result.executive_bottom_line: The authentication flow creates real signed-in sessions from identity material that the requester can supply or read back, so public callers complete login without proving phone or Google account ownership.

published_flaws.title: Authentication endpoints issue sessions without verified identity proof
published_flaws.bottom_line: OTP requests return the verification code to the requester, and Google sign-in accepts caller-supplied or fabricated profiles, so an unauthenticated visitor completes login and receives a persisted authenticated session.
published_flaws.business_capability: Mobile and Google authentication for the weather dashboard

trigger.statement: A visitor uses the public OTP or Google sign-in endpoints and supplies the identity material that the same flow exposes or accepts.

observed_behavior.statement: The OTP path returns the generated code in the request flow and the Google path accepts a posted or synthesized profile, then the backend records login state and returns a JWT-backed success response.

business_rule.statement: Sign-in must require proof of control of the phone number or a verified Google identity before a session token and user record are created.

business_impact.immediate_outcome: The service returns successful login responses, issues JWT-backed sessions, and writes login state for identities that were not verified by an external proof step.
business_impact.affected_party_or_asset: Authenticated dashboard access, persisted user profiles, login counters, and user-linked history state.
business_impact.business_downside: Unauthenticated visitors obtain signed-in access and creates or update persisted account state under chosen phone or Google identities.
business_impact.scale_mechanism: The behavior is reachable through public authentication endpoints and completes in the normal sign-in workflow.
business_impact.detection_difficulty: Successful responses and normal login records look the same as legitimate sign-ins.
business_impact.reversibility: Issued sessions expire later, but created profiles, login counters, and stored history require explicit cleanup.

business_path_nodes.business_label: Identity proof is caller-supplied or returned to the same requester
Backend accepts sign-in and records login
Session token and persisted user profile
Unverified user gains authenticated access and alters account state

code_path_explanation: The backend exposes public POST routes for /api/auth/send-otp, /api/auth/verify-otp, and /api/auth/google.

The OTP send handler returns the service result from createAndSendOtp, and that service includes the generated code in its returned object; the frontend also reads backendRes.code and surfaces it in the request flow.
The OTP verify handler only checks that the submitted code matches the stored session, then records login state and returns a JWT and user object.

The Google login flow posts either the Firebase popup result or a synthesized fallback profile to the backend, and the backend accepts req.body.profile or creates its own default profile, records login, signs a JWT, and returns success.

counterevidence_checked.item_checked: OTP verification requires an active session, an unexpired code, and an exact code match.
counterevidence_checked.result: Those checks validate the same code that the request flow returns to the requester.

counterevidence_checked.item_checked: Google popup close handling returns a failed client response.
counterevidence_checked.result: Only the user-closed popup branch returns failure; other popup failures fall back to a synthesized profile, and the backend also defaults a profile when none is supplied.

published_flaws.control_objective: Require independently verified identity evidence before issuing an authenticated session or persisting login state.

acceptance_check.given: an unauthenticated caller who can reach the public authentication endpoints
acceptance_check.when: the caller reads the OTP from the request flow or submits a fabricated Google profile and completes the corresponding sign-in request, the application returns a successful authenticated response and records the login as that identity.
acceptance_check.then: the sign-in is rejected unless the caller presents externally verified proof for the claimed phone number or Google account

result.decision_summary: Published one high-severity authentication flaw. Both supplied candidates converge on the same reachable business failure: public auth endpoints trust identity material that is exposed to or chosen by the requester, and then issue authenticated sessions and persisted login state.
